Customers range from residential clients in Idaho and surrounding areas to commercial accounts such as restaurants and offices. Projects have included a large bookcase for a home, a bar top for a commercial space, and custom cutting boards for gifts.

Barrett emphasizes handcrafted methods and responsible material use as a response to mass-produced furniture. The company positions its work as heirloom-quality pieces built to last generations, with design guidance provided throughout the process.

Boulder Furniture Arts, founded in 1985, operates from Boulder, Colorado. The company has built a reputation over nearly four decades as a fine furniture design-and-build studio.

The firm produces two primary lines: BFA Classic, a collection of time-honored designs largely unchanged since its inception, and BFA Create, a custom arm that develops one-off pieces, live-edge slabs, built-ins, and full installations. Work flows through an in-house process that includes concept development, CAD drawings and renderings, fabrication under a one-person-one-piece model, hand-rubbed oil finishing, and custom finish matching. The shop also offers commercial-grade options, built-and-brought delivery, full-service installation, and a lifetime guarantee backed by repair, refinishing, and disassembly services.

Clients range from architects who value precision to the 64th of an inch, interior designers seeking seamless collaboration, and residential customers furnishing homes with locally sourced hardwoods. The company also serves commercial leaders, artists, and environmentally conscious buyers who track carbon storage in their furnishings.

Boulder Furniture Arts distinguishes itself by sourcing all materials within a two-day drive of its shop, maintaining a ten-year apprenticeship program, and avoiding surplus inventory. The company describes itself as an old-school working art house run by people who give a damn, emphasizing analog modern design and playful restraint.

name: Boxcar Woody (Reclaimed Lumber)
old_description: During those pioneering years, one car stood out among the rest, almost as important as the locomotive engine itself: the boxcar. Not just because of the versatility for the freight it could carry, but because of the connection with humanity it offered. The typical boxcar doubled as a passenger car for the ticketless. It was even sometimes left behind in those newly founded towns as a shelter or, for others, a home. It provided an escape for those wanting to run from his or her current predicament or a ride to a better life. Often, the boxcar’s walls were a sounding board for a newly penned song or where a life drew its very first and, sometimes, sadly, last breath. The American Boxcar was all of this and more to both early Americans and Immigrants alike.
about:
Boxcar Woody operates from Stockyards City in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. The business traces its roots to 2015, when a road trip to harvest materials from retired American boxcars sparked the creation of Boxcar Revival, which later evolved into Boxcar Woody.

The company reclaims authentic freight materials—boxcar flooring, cargo planks, and whiskey barrel staves—and processes them in its Oklahoma workshop. Operations include selecting, milling, and finishing reclaimed lumber to produce raw materials such as countertop slabs, mantels, and flooring, as well as finished goods like dining tables, chairs, barstools, lighting fixtures, and barn doors. Each piece is handcrafted, and custom sizing is available for made-to-order projects.

Projects range from whole-house remodels featuring countertops, sliding doors, and vanities to custom barn doors and hospitality installations such as bars with waterfall edges. Testimonials reference clients in Oklahoma and beyond who have used the material for furniture, countertops, and architectural elements.

The company states its mission is to preserve the history of American railways by giving retired boxcar materials new life in modern spaces. It emphasizes quality, craftsmanship, and the uniqueness of each piece, noting that no two tables are alike because the wood carries the character of its original service.

about:
Boyko Inc. was established in August 1987 in Stanton, North Dakota, by brothers Ron and Tom Boyko as a USDA-inspected food manufacturing plant producing bakery and meat products. The family-owned corporation quickly expanded its product development and manufacturing services for a variety of clients.

After years of growth, the company began upgrading its own equipment and found a market for the used machinery it replaced. In 1996 Boyko Inc. started buying and selling used food processing equipment, and by 2002 it had transitioned to full-time equipment dealing while still running the manufacturing plant. The manufacturing division was sold in 2006 to focus entirely on the used equipment business. Today the firm operates as a dealer and service provider, offering auctions, liquidations, consignment sales, asset management, process and plant system consulting, and technical support for food processing equipment.

The company serves food manufacturers and processors across the industry, helping them acquire or dispose of equipment ranging from bakery and packaging lines to conveyors, freezers, and mixers. Its customer base includes plants seeking individual machines, complete production lines, or turnkey liquidation services.

Drawing on its manufacturing heritage, Boyko Inc. emphasizes a practical understanding of processors' operational challenges. Its stated mission is to provide efficient, reliable service with integrity as a family-owned leader in the food processing sector.

about:
Branded Screen Printing & Embroidery was founded in 2009 in Reno, Nevada, as a locally owned and operated shop focused on simplifying custom apparel for area businesses, schools, teams, and events. The company began on Moana Lane with the goal of keeping production in-house to maintain quality and speed, a model it still follows today.

The company provides a full range of decoration services including screen printing, embroidery, direct-to-film (DTF/UCP) printing, promotional products, vinyl decals, signs and banners, trade show displays, graphic design, jersey sublimation, online company stores, and contract printing. All production is handled at its Reno facility, allowing control over quality and turnaround. The shop serves both local customers in Reno, Sparks, and Carson City and ships orders nationwide.

Its customer base spans businesses needing work shirts, polos, jackets, and uniforms; K-12 schools ordering spirit wear and fundraiser items; youth and adult sports teams requiring jerseys and practice gear; nonprofits producing volunteer and event apparel; event organizers sourcing staff shirts, giveaways, and banners; and industrial crews in construction, trades, and warehouses seeking hi-vis and durable workwear.

Branded emphasizes in-house production as a differentiator, citing faster communication, consistent quality, and a standard turnaround of five to seven business days after proof approval, with rush options available. Screen printing minimums start at 12 pieces, and some decoration methods have no minimums. Every order includes a digital proof before production, and customers work directly with branding advisors for design support, apparel selection, and timeline management.

name: Bridgeport Insulated Wire Co
old_description: . From magnet wire and Litz wire to military-specification insulations, Bridgeport Insulated Wire delivers the quality and precision your applications demand.
about:
Bridgeport Insulated Wire Co. has operated from Bridgeport, Connecticut since its founding in 1950. The company was established as a U.S.-based manufacturer of precision insulated wire and has maintained domestic production at its Connecticut facility for over seven decades.

The company produces a range of insulated wire products including magnet wire, Litz wire, textile-served wire, and custom bobbin-wound constructions. Its capabilities cover enamel insulation application (with over 12 insulation types from Class 105 to Class 220), wire drawing, tinning, stranding, twisting, and textile serving using fibers such as glass, Nomex, and Kevlar. All machinery is designed and built in-house by the company's engineering staff.

Bridgeport Insulated Wire serves manufacturers in the electrical, aerospace, instrumentation, consumer electronics, motor, and defense sectors. Its wire is specified for transformers, solenoids, fractional motors, synchros, relays, aircraft systems, and military equipment where reliability is critical.

The company emphasizes its military and government approvals—including NEMA MW-1000 compliance, Naval JW-1177/A approval, and UL-listed insulations—as well as its fully domestic supply chain, which it says keeps quality high, lead times short, and communication direct. An in-house engineering department consults on insulation selection and government specification compliance.

Brooks Molds is based in Elmore, Alabama. The company specializes in the tooling and manufacturing of molds for the cast polymer industry, including cultured marble, Tyvarian, and solid surface applications. These clients rely on the molds for daily production of cultured marble and solid surface products.

The company emphasizes skill and durability as differentiators, citing over 20 years in the cast polymer mold business, immaculate care of permanent master patterns, and the ability to handle both standard and custom design challenges. Their heavy-duty bracing systems are designed to reduce downtime from mold repairs, and they claim their molds last for years under heavy use.

about:
C.R. International Inc. (CRI) is a woman-owned small business headquartered in Laurel, Maryland. Founded in 1981, the company began as a small engineering firm supplying communications and data-processing equipment to federal customers, including protocol adapters and specialized radio/telephone interface devices.

Today CRI operates as a full-service electronic manufacturing services (EMS) provider from an 18,000-square-foot, climate-controlled facility. The shop runs two surface-mount technology lines equipped with DEK screen printers and Mycronic pick-and-place machines capable of placing 01005 components through large BGAs, and offers paste printing, conformal coating (acrylic, silicone, epoxy), box-build electro-mechanical assembly, functional testing, first-article inspection, and component verification. Services span prototype development to volume production, supported by AEGIS manufacturing software for work instructions and process control.

CRI serves aerospace and flight programs, defense and military agencies, communications, industrial, medical, and commercial customers, as well as start-ups. Notable references include NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory—where CRI-populated boards supported pyrotechnic activation on a test flight—and Department of Defense prime contractors who rely on the company for tactical electronics.

The company emphasizes partnership and high-reliability manufacturing, maintaining IPC Class III as its standard process, with personnel trained to J-STD-001 and IPC-A-610, including flight-certified soldering and inspection. Certifications include ISO 9001:2015, ITAR registration, CMMC Level 2 C3PAO, and RoHS compliance, reflecting a focus on mission-critical quality and data security.

Founded in 1990 in Fargo, North Dakota, CI Sport began as a start-up screen-print company conceived by entrepreneurs Randy Thorson and Warren Ackley. The pair, who were involved in the hospitality industry, created the business to outfit bars and restaurants with decorated uniforms, apparel, and souvenirs. From that small beginning, the company grew into a nationally recognized supplier of decorated apparel with three operating divisions: CI Apparel, CI Sport, and CI Tourism.

Today, CI Sport operates a 73,000-square-foot, state-of-the-art facility in southwest Fargo that houses all decoration production, sales, art creation, digitizing, and inventory under one roof—a rarity in the industry. The company’s core decoration processes are embroidery and screen printing, supported by in-house art and digitizing services. CI Sport serves more than 700 college bookstores across 49 states, manages over 25 e-commerce uniform programs, and operates concept shops and T-shirt towers at collegiate and minor-league venues nationwide.

The collegiate division, CI Sport, holds over 300 licenses and supplies college bookstores, arenas, and sporting-goods stores in all 50 states, while also serving as a local license vendor for several NHL and NBA teams and minor-league baseball and hockey fan shops. The corporate division, CI Apparel, provides custom decorated apparel to businesses across virtually every industry, offering access to brands such as Nike, OGIO, and Columbia. The tourism division, CI Tourism, produces custom resort, lake, and cabin apparel with low minimum orders.

CI Sport emphasizes its fully integrated in-house operation, low minimum orders (12 pieces for embroidery reorders and tourism, 36 pieces for screen printing), and fast turnaround times as key differentiators. The company was built on the premise of controlling every step from design to delivery to ensure quality and speed for collegiate, corporate, and tourism customers.

old_description: All products from California Plastix are inspected for quality and consistency by trained employees.  Nothing leaves our factory without inspection.
about:
California Plastix operates from Pomona, California, in the heart of Southern California's manufacturing corridor. The company was founded on the principle of delivering reliable, American-made packaging with the flexibility to meet any customer's needs, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed. Ownership details such as family, veteran, or woman-owned status are not stated.

All manufacturing occurs in-house across three integrated departments: extrusion, flexographic printing, and converting. Extrusion lines produce film at widths from 5 to 70 inches layflat and gauges from 0.75 to 8 mil, with a typical tolerance of ±5%. Flexographic presses handle up to six colors with a registration tolerance of ±1/32 inch and repeat lengths of 4 to 24 inches. Converting equipment fabricates side-weld, bottom-seal, gusseted, wicketed, zipper, and tape bags in widths of 3 to 60 inches and lengths of 4 to 72 inches, with wicket counts of 250 to 1,000 bags per wicket. The facility also produces tubing, sheeting, centerfold film, and roll stock.

California Plastix serves food and beverage processors, bakeries, produce packers, industrial manufacturers, retail and e-commerce packagers, medical and pharmaceutical suppliers, agricultural and horticultural operations, and commercial wholesale distributors. Its products are used in supply chains for major retailers such as Costco, The Home Depot, Trader Joe's, Target, and Bloomingdale's, though the company notes it is not affiliated with or endorsed by those brands.

The company emphasizes its fully integrated Southern California facility as a differentiator, enabling faster turnaround, direct communication with production staff, and consistent quality control. Quotes are typically provided within 24 hours, and the company ships nationwide from Pomona. Its mission centers on dependable, high-quality poly packaging that helps businesses operate efficiently and keep supply chains moving.

about:
Carolina Foods was founded in 1934 in Charlotte, North Carolina, and has operated continuously as a maker of sweet baked goods for over 90 years. The company maintains its headquarters in Charlotte and runs a modern baking facility in nearby Pineville, NC.

The company produces a range of sweet baked goods including gem donuts, donut sticks, honey buns, fritters, cinnamon rolls, and mini pies under its Duchess brand and as a private-label and co-manufacturing partner. All products are made from scratch using time-honored techniques combined with technology; the Pineville plant features automated packaging from Schubert and was named Food Engineering’s 2025 Plant of the Year.

Customers include retailers across convenience, grocery, mass-market, and club channels, as well as quick-serve and hospitality food-service operators. The company positions itself as a bakery partner of choice for brands seeking customized sweet baked goods and scalable co-manufacturing solutions.

Carolina Foods traces its differentiation to early innovations—it claims to be the first to crack extended shelf life for sweet baked goods and the first to introduce the honey bun—and to its in-house control of every production step, which it says enables faster innovation, gold-standard quality and safety 365 days a year, and unmatched service.

old_description: As a 4th Generation family-owned business, Carolina Textiles is a descendant of Grossman Industries, which was founded in 1920 in Columbus, Ohio.
about:
Carolina Textiles, headquartered in Walterboro, South Carolina, traces its roots to 1920 when Grossman Industries was founded in Columbus, Ohio. Now a fourth-generation family-owned business, the company began as a rag operation and has expanded through acquisitions: the Walterboro location opened in 1995, the Greer facility was added in 2013 via the purchase of American Wiping Cloth, and the Atlanta site came in 2016 with the acquisition of Mountain Textiles.

The company manufactures and distributes cleaning cloths, towels, disposable wipers, and wiping rags in materials such as colored knit, fleece, terry cloth, paper, and microfiber. It offers hand-packed and machine-compressed packaging in 5-, 10-, 25-, and 50-pound boxes or bags. Across its three Southeast locations, Carolina Textiles diverts more than 12 million pounds of used textiles from landfills each year, repurposing them into wiping products.

Customers span automotive, marine, industrial, janitorial, and food-service sectors. The firm sells primarily through a distributor network across South Carolina, North Carolina, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Tennessee, Mississippi, Alabama, and Virginia, and also runs a thrift-store partnership program that converts unsalable donations into revenue.

Management emphasizes its green heritage—recycling textiles since the business began—and a service model built on extensive product lines, convenient ordering, competitive pricing, and fast delivery, backed by a team with over 40 years of industry experience.

about:
Carris Reels Inc. was founded in 1951 in Rutland, Vermont, by Henry Carris, who built the business on a culture of operational excellence summarized by the phrase “get the wood out.” His son, Bill Carris, expanded the company through acquisitions and new plants in the 1980s. In 1995 Bill began converting the company to an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP); the ESOP became majority owner in 2005 and reached 100% employee ownership in 2008. The corporate headquarters is now in Fincastle, Virginia.

The company manufactures wood reels (plywood, nailed wood, hardboard), plastic reels (standard, fine‑wire, welding‑wire, and magnet‑wire types), and recycled reels, and provides reel assembly, recycling, repair, and distribution services. Operations are vertically integrated across multiple facilities in Vermont, Virginia, California, Indiana, Connecticut, North Carolina, Texas, Arkansas, Canada (Ontario, Alberta, Quebec, Saskatchewan), and Mexico. Capabilities include plastic molding and extrusion, resin processing, machining, tube‑winding, stamped‑metal reel production, and fabrication of chocks, blocks, and lagging.

Carris serves the wire and cable packaging industry, supplying reels for fine wire, magnet wire, insulated wire, and welding wire. Customers include manufacturers of electrical and communication cable who rely on the company’s reel assembly, recycling, and logistics programs.

Carris emphasizes its employee‑owned structure and vertically integrated model as competitive advantages that benefit customers. The recycled‑reel program is promoted as an eco‑friendly option that reduces disposal and shipping costs.

name: Carson Manufacturing Inc
old_description: After 48 years of operations, the company is well-known, a leading manufacturer of planetary gearheads. And, of course, the innovation didn’t stop in 1996.
about:
Carson Manufacturing operates from Carson City, Nevada, where it was founded in 1986. The family-owned business traces its roots to Eddie Capps, who purchased the company with his wife Barbara; their daughter Delores Stacy now serves as vice president and her son Kenny Penn as sales engineer. In 1996, the three-generation team introduced a breakthrough redesign that replaced the traditional housing with a bearing holder, creating concentric force alignment that became an industry standard.

The company produces planetary gearheads across five product lines—Precision, Eliminator, 'S', Right Angle, and fully custom units—with over 231 standard models and ratios up to 10,000:1. An internal R&D division develops and strenuously tests every design under varied conditions. Standard gearheads ship within two days; custom designs with set parameters are delivered in a week. All manufacturing is performed in-house in the United States.

Customers span medical device makers using gearheads for cancer detection, paper manufacturers improving production equipment, aerospace programs such as Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, motion-control specialists like Servo Systems Co., HVAC firms including MAS HVAC, and automation integrators such as In-Position Technologies. The client base ranges from university research labs to industrial OEMs.

Carson Manufacturing was built on the premise that custom gearhead engineering should not carry a design fee. The firm’s differentiators include free custom design, rigorous in-house testing, a commitment to on-time and on-budget delivery, and a 100% U.S.-made product that avoids tariffs and overseas shipping delays.

The shop’s NTEA membership connects it to the broader work‑truck industry and keeps it current with commercial‑vehicle standards.

Central Cable serves the telecommunications, broadband, and fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) sectors. Notable projects include a 48-mile fiber network for South Slope Cooperative Communications in Iowa and an 89-mile rural FTTH build for CTC Technology connecting 270 homes. The company states its mission is to relentlessly pursue industry leadership in quality and production while keeping customer relationships as the top priority. The company specializes in custom plastic injection molding, operating presses ranging from 7 to 460 tons. It provides a full suite of services including mold design and manufacturing, part design and engineering, assembly, packaging, and third-party logistics. A Class 7 cleanroom supports medical component production.

Central Custom Molding serves medical, defense, consumer electronics, automation, and homegoods markets. Its parts have been used in medical devices produced in a Class 7 cleanroom, on the submersible that reached the Mariana Trench, on corporate jets, in autonomous aircraft, and in water filtration systems for developing regions.

The company positions itself as a strategic partner rather than a vendor, emphasizing its central U.S. location to mitigate supply chain disruptions from natural disasters or geopolitical instability. It also promotes reshoring, leveraging its multi-generational U.S. manufacturing experience.

about:
Central Sheet Metal Products, Inc. has operated from Skokie, Illinois since 1912. The company was founded as a Chicago storefront supplying copper, roof flashings, gutters and downspouts, and has remained in the Silverstein family for five generations. Current leadership includes fourth‑generation owners Joel and Peter Silverstein and fifth‑generation owners Ron and Rob Silverstein.

The shop specializes in precision sheet metal fabrication, offering fiber laser cutting with lights‑out automation, CNC punching and forming, welding, drilling/tapping, hardware insertion, polishing and contract finishing (powder coating, e‑coating, painting, silk screening, plating and anodizing). Engineering is performed in‑house using SolidWorks 3D modeling, with design, reverse‑engineering and re‑engineering services. The facility runs multiple press brakes (up to 135 metric tons), a Mitsubishi 2.5 kW fiber laser with a 120″ × 60″ bed, Strippit turret punches, and a range of secondary equipment. The company handles small, medium and large volume runs and multiple part‑mix OEM programs.

Customers span OEM medical and dental devices, electronics, rack‑mount and audio/visual enclosures, computer peripherals, industrial equipment, electrical and air‑handling systems, display/POP, gaming, food‑and‑beverage vending, and agricultural machinery. The firm focuses on contract manufacturing for original equipment manufacturers.

The company emphasizes quality craftsmanship, complete customer satisfaction, direct communication, on‑time delivery and continuous improvement. Capital investments in automation and calibration have reduced lead times, and a business‑continuity mindset aims to maintain consistent service across generations.

about:
Champion Petfoods USA, headquartered in Auburn, Kentucky, traces its origins to 1985 when the company was founded in a small town in Alberta, Canada. The business began with a singular focus on crafting premium pet food and has since expanded to serve pet owners in more than 90 countries worldwide.

The company manufactures two primary brands, ORIJEN and ACANA, for dogs and cats. Its process centers on sourcing WholePrey animal ingredients — meat, poultry, and fish — from a curated supplier network, which are then formulated by Ph.D.-level nutrition experts and veterinarians and produced in what the company describes as state-of-the-art kitchens. ORIJEN recipes contain up to 90 percent animal ingredients, while ACANA balances protein-rich animal ingredients with whole fruits and vegetables.

Champion serves the premium pet food industry globally, with a presence across three major geographic regions. Its customer base includes independent and neighborhood pet retailers, supported through a founding sponsorship of IndiePet, as well as direct consumer sales. The company also collaborates with the University of Guelph on pet nutrition science.

The company states that its exclusive focus on premium pet food allows it to perfect recipes and innovate new products, emphasizing that it never adds wheat, corn, or soy in its kitchens. Its stated mission is to provide peak nutrition, optimal nourishment, and ultimate flavor so pet lovers can feel confident feeding their dogs and cats.

about:
Cherry Brook Woodworks operates from Canton, Connecticut, where in 2001 the Aleksa family purchased a home in the historic district and converted two antique apple barns into a woodworking shop.

The shop produces custom furniture, museum-quality antique reproductions, and repair and restoration services for heirloom pieces, all made by hand using traditional joinery and period-appropriate finishes. The workspace remains in the original barn structures on the family property, and the output ranges from one-off commissions to a rotating catalog of original designs such as Shaker tripod tables, sideboards, and chests crafted in tiger maple, birdseye maple, cherry, white oak, and walnut.

Clients include individual homeowners, interior designers, architects, and museums, with pieces shipped throughout the United States. The company has reproduced historic furniture from photographs or originals for institutional clients and restored family heirlooms for private owners.

Aleksa emphasizes a collaborative process, listening closely to each client to create furniture that fits specific spaces and styles, a level of personal involvement he contrasts with larger production shops. His approach stems from a belief that the relationship with the client is as important as the finished piece, and that honoring the materials and history behind each project results in furniture built to last generations.

name: Chilton Furniture
old_description: We offer a unique collection of designs celebrating natural materials, New England aesthetics, and quality craftsmanship.
about:
Chilton Furniture traces its roots to 1885 when Chilton Manufacturing Co. was established in Portland, Maine, producing paints, varnishes, and industrial coatings. The business was acquired by the Martens family in 1936, shifting focus to stains and finishes for furniture makers. In 2014, the Levin family took ownership, refocusing the company on exclusive furniture designs crafted from domestically sourced North American hardwoods. Today, it operates as a family-owned brand headquartered in Portland, with a flagship showroom there and a second location in Freeport.

The company designs contemporary, functional furniture—including seating, tables, storage, beds, and accessories—and collaborates with a network of independent makers in Maine and the Midwest to handcraft each piece from premium domestic hardwoods such as cherry, maple, walnut, and white oak. All materials are sourced in the United States. Chilton provides nationwide delivery and backs its products with a lifetime warranty for the original owner.

Chilton serves both direct consumers and trade professionals, including interior designers and retailers, through a trade partner program that offers discounts and benefits. Its furniture is marketed for residential use, with collections such as Shaker, Hudson, and Maine Made appealing to customers seeking handcrafted, domestically produced pieces.

The brand emphasizes its commitment to enduring craftsmanship, domestic sourcing, and New England design heritage. The lifetime warranty reflects confidence in the durability of its furniture, while the maker-partnership model aims to sustain regional woodworking traditions.

For more than 130 years, we’ve been conducting business in a way that’s good for our customers, respectful to our employees and compassionate toward animals.
about:
Clemens Food Group was founded more than 130 years ago in Hatfield, Pennsylvania, and remains a sixth-generation, family-owned business. The company traces its roots to a small independent operation that has grown into a vertically coordinated pork supplier while maintaining its original commitment to ethics, integrity, and stewardship.

Today the company operates across the full pork supply chain: feed milling, a network of over 250 company-owned and independent family farms in Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, and Pennsylvania, and three pork processing facilities in Hatfield and Tyrone, Pennsylvania, and Coldwater, Michigan. Its logistics and transportation division moves live hogs from farms and finished products to customers. The portfolio includes the Hatfield®, Farm Promise®, Prima Porta®, and Kunzler® brands, the latter added in May 2024.

Clemens serves customers of all sizes, from independent foodservice operators to large retail and food manufacturing accounts, providing branded and custom pork programs. Its Country View Family Farms division ensures a consistent supply of hogs raised under aligned animal-welfare and biosecurity standards.

The company emphasizes that vertical coordination gives it control over quality and sustainability from farm to fork. Its Farm Promise® line offers No Antibiotics Ever pork, and the organization highlights transparent, compassionate animal care as a core differentiator.

name: Click Therapeutics
old_description: ™, and founded Click Therapeutics, which develops, validates, and commercializes software as prescription medical treatments for people with unmet medical needs.
about:
Click Therapeutics is headquartered in New York, New York. Founded in 2012 by David Benshoof Klein, who recognized the impact of smartphones on behavior and cognition and began developing mobile-application-based treatments, coining the term "Digital Therapeutics™." The company is backed by biotech and pharma investors including HIG, Accelmed, and Sanofi Ventures.

The company develops, validates, and commercializes software as prescription medical treatments. Its multimodal platform, Click SE™, combines software with pharmacotherapy to create software-enhanced drug treatments. The team spans clinicians, researchers, and technologists who conduct clinical trials and manage regulatory submissions.

Click Therapeutics serves the life sciences, digital health, and medical device industries, working with pharmaceutical partners such as Otsuka to co-develop prescription digital therapeutics. Its treatments are prescribed by physicians and reimbursed as drug-software combination products, targeting patients with unmet needs in psychiatry, neurology, metabolic disease, and oncology.

The company was started to leverage software to improve clinical outcomes and bridge gaps in treatment access, aiming to provide patients everywhere access to safe and effective prescription digital therapeutics. Its differentiators include an AI-enabled platform, a first FDA-cleared prescription app for adjunctive MDD treatment developed with Otsuka, and a pipeline spanning multiple therapeutic areas.

name: ClickFold Plastics
old_description: All we need is a sketch, CAD file, mock-up, or the internal components to design your part or product. We can also reverse-engineer injection molded parts, or sheet metal housings.
about:
ClickFold Plastics was founded in 2001 in Charlotte, North Carolina, to address a gap in the market for custom plastic enclosures and parts in smaller volumes. The company operates from a facility on the North Carolina–South Carolina border near Charlotte Douglas International Airport, providing convenient logistics for domestic and cross-border shipments.

The company specializes in a zero-tooling fabrication process that produces custom plastic housings, enclosures, covers, panels, holders, spacers, lenses, bezels, guards, bumpers, and insulators without the need for injection molds. Core capabilities include CNC machining, 3D printing, digital graphics and UV printing, EMI shielding, assembly, packaging, custom kitting, and virtual prototyping. The process is geared toward low-volume production runs and just-in-time delivery, with a typical concept-to-production timeline of under four weeks.

ClickFold serves OEMs across industrial controls, medical devices, communications, gaming and simulators, building controls, measuring equipment, government and military, and commercial vehicles. Customers are typically companies that require custom plastic parts in smaller quantities delivered on a just-in-time basis, with support for rapid product development and prototyping.

The business was started to offer a cost-effective alternative to injection molding for low-volume needs and a more refined option than sheet metal forming. Its stated differentiators are the elimination of tooling costs, no minimum order quantities, fast turnaround, and ISO 9001 certification maintained since 2017.

about:
Clore Automotive, LLC is based in Overland Park, Kansas. The company was founded in 2001, building on an over 50-year heritage in the automotive equipment aftermarket.

The company designs, develops, and manufactures a range of automotive service equipment, including jump starters, battery chargers, battery testers, maintainers, and work lights. Its product portfolio is organized under well-known brands such as Booster PAC, Jump-N-Carry, SOLAR, CHARGE IT!, Light-N-Carry, and PRO-LOGIX. Specific offerings include 12-volt portable jump starters, 100-amp flashing power supplies, 60/40/10-amp battery chargers, digital battery and system testers with integrated printers, and lithium jump starters. The company also provides technical support and repair services through its customer care and technical service teams.

Clore Automotive serves both professional technicians and consumers across the automotive aftermarket. Its equipment is used in professional service facilities and by individual vehicle owners. The company emphasizes meeting the evolving power needs of modern vehicles, with products optimized for a wide variety of battery types found in today's vehicles.

The company differentiates itself through a focus on durability and longevity, stating that its products are built to exceed the rigorous demands of professional technicians and perform in tough environments long after competing products have failed. It also highlights superior customer care, with technical service teams that can diagnose problems, expedite parts, and refer customers to service centers. Continuous innovation in jump starter battery technology and a steady stream of new products addressing specific technician needs are cited as core drivers.

The firm’s building packages have been used for projects ranging from small storage structures to large commercial facilities, and its materials meet ASTM standards for fencing and other applications.

about:
Coastal Plastic Molding Inc. was founded in 1984 in Alvin, Texas, just south of Houston. The company began as a small family-owned operation and has remained under family ownership throughout its growth.

The firm provides full-service plastic manufacturing, including injection molding of thermoplastic parts, extrusion, in-house tooling and mold making, design engineering support, prototyping, short-run and high-volume production, and secondary operations such as trimming, drilling, assembly, and packaging. Its 20,000-square-foot facility runs molding operations 24 hours a day, equipped with electric and hydraulic presses, including a 180-ton JSW all-electric machine and MATSIU material dryers.

Coastal serves a broad range of industries across the United States, including pharmaceutical and medical, aerospace, construction, industrial, electronics, consumer products, geophysical, and filtration. Customers range from prototype developers to large-scale OEMs.

The company emphasizes its Texas-based, family-owned identity as a differentiator, highlighting in-house tooling to avoid overseas dependencies, electric molding technology that reduces waste and energy consumption, an independent quality control department, and a commitment to transparent communication and local job retention.

name: Coldstream Power
old_description: Coldstream Power helps clients reduce their energy costs & carbon footprints.
about:
Coldstream Power is based in Milford, Ohio, and was founded in 2006. The company operates as a locally owned small business under the Coldstream Companies umbrella, which was started by Jon Davis. It began with a goal of helping homeowners in the Milford and greater Cincinnati area take control of their energy futures and find cost savings on utility bills while increasing sustainability.

The firm provides solar panel design and installation for both rooftop and ground-mounted systems, generator installation (primarily Generac units), EV charger installation compatible with any vehicle make, and electrical panel upgrades. Coldstream Power handles the full project lifecycle in-house — from consultation and custom design using modeling software to installation and activation — and notes that most solar installations are completed within one to two days. The team carries over two decades of combined experience in residential and commercial projects across the Cincinnati region.

Coldstream Power serves residential and commercial customers throughout greater Cincinnati, including communities such as Mason, West Chester, Blue Ash, and Morrow. Project examples cited on its site include a 5.6 kW system with REC400 panels in Miamisburg, a 10 kW system with Enphase batteries and microinverters in Milford, and a 53-panel array in Morrow.

The company emphasizes that it never uses subcontractors, relies on an in-house design team, and installs products from brands such as REC, Meyer Burger, Enphase, and Generac. Transparent pricing, free consultations, and flexible financing options — including $0-down solar — are presented as core differentiators, along with a commitment to honesty and customer satisfaction reflected in consistently high review ratings.

name: Cole Wire & Cable Co
old_description: A trusted distributor of high-quality wire and cable products since 1979, Cole Wire is a family-owned and operated company, built on our reputation for personalized service, fast turnaround, and a deep understanding of what keeps your projects moving.
about:
Cole Wire & Cable Co. is headquartered in Lincolnshire, Illinois, with additional sales offices in Ohio. The company was founded in 1979 by Shel and Teri Cole and remains family-owned, now led by second-generation owner Leo Cole. Over more than four decades it has grown into one of the nation's largest master stocking distributors of specialty electrical and electronic wire and cable, serving customers across the United States and internationally in Canada, Mexico, the United Kingdom, and China.

The company operates a 26,000-square-foot combined office and warehouse that houses a multi-million-dollar inventory of products such as portable cord, tray cable, hook-up wire, armored cable, power cable, low-voltage wire, and electronic wire and cable. Beyond distribution, Cole Wire provides an extensive suite of in-house value-added services — cut-to-length, stripping, labeling, bundling, custom coloring, custom striping, custom printing, twisting, kitting, crimping, harness building, design/build/stocking programs, and re-spooling. It also runs a custom manufacturing division producing wire harnesses, cord sets, coil cords, and tailored assemblies for OEM, automotive, aerospace, and industrial applications, with scalable production from prototype to full-scale runs. All processes are backed by ISO 9001 certification.

Cole Wire serves a broad range of industries. Its OEM and manufacturing customers receive precise wire configurations bundled and stripped for fast, consistent builds. Construction and electrical contractors rely on custom-cut, labeled cable and stocked product ready to ship. Marine and offshore clients get rugged, corrosion-resistant cable for shipboard and facility use. Specialty contractors in remediation, pumps, conveyors, and high-temperature environments also source custom heavy-duty solutions. The company additionally supports automotive, aerospace, and general industrial sectors.

The firm's stated mission is to provide solutions that earn greater efficiencies for its customers. It emphasizes personalized service, technical expertise, and flexible customization — offering same-day shipping on stocked items, no cut charges, and full in-house control over quality and turnaround. This focus on reliability and service, shaped by integrity and responsive communication, is presented as the core differentiator.

With over 20 years of experience in West Denver and Jefferson County, the team provides end-to-end electrical scope from service calls to complex multi-unit installations.

Customers range from homeowners preparing for electrification to property managers of multi-family complexes and general contractors seeking a reliable electrical partner. The company also works closely with local plumbing and HVAC contractors who rely on its code-compliant connections for their own projects. Every technician sent to a job site holds an individual state license and insurance coverage.

All installations are backed by a three-year workmanship warranty, reflecting the founder’s emphasis on clear communication and lasting craftsmanship.

about:
Columbus Machine Works operates from Columbus, Ohio, where it was founded in 1997 by Mike Stacey. Stacey, who holds a Bachelor of Science in Industrial Design, began as a job-shop machinist commuting by bicycle to serve local customers. His deep-rooted passion for machinery and manufacturing grew the business into a central Ohio hub for machining, metalwork, and craftsmanship.

The shop provides a full range of machining and fabrication services, including CNC milling (up to 84" x 32" x 30"), CNC turning (up to 20" diameter x 48" long), wire EDM, conventional machining, gear cutting, grinding, welding (TIG, MIG, stick, spray), and structural fabrication. Services also cover reverse engineering, on-site evaluation, inventory stocking, pickup and delivery, and 24/7 emergency breakdown response.

While the company serves a broad base of local manufacturers, its listed industry focus includes medical equipment. Customers range from small shops needing prototype parts to larger operations requiring OEM replacement components, jigs, fixtures, and repair of shafts, gears, and bearings.

Columbus Machine Works positions itself as a cost-effective alternative to factory replacement parts, emphasizing competitive pricing, lead times, and a one-stop-shop model. The founder's original vision — blending traditional craftsmanship with modern machining — remains the stated differentiator, supported by capabilities like emergency service, inventory management, and on-site support.

about:
Consolidated Telcom, based in Dickinson, North Dakota, traces its roots to January 2, 1961, when the Bowman-Slope Rural Telephone Mutual Aid Corporation and the Dunn Telephone Mutual Aid Corporation merged to form the Consolidated Telephone Cooperative. The cooperative is owned by its members—customers who use its services—and operates as a not-for-profit entity serving southwestern North Dakota.

The cooperative delivers voice, video, and data services across 19 rural communities and the Dickinson area, operating a 100% fiber-to-the-home network in its cooperative exchanges and a hybrid fiber-coax system in Dickinson. Its wholly owned subsidiaries provide competitive local exchange (CLEC) service, internet access, and cable television. Consolidated has invested millions of dollars in network infrastructure since its founding.

Customers include residential subscribers in communities such as Amidon, Dodge, Dunn Center, and Bowman; businesses in Dickinson, Belfield, and Gladstone; and institutions like Dickinson State University, which was the cooperative’s first CLEC customer. The cooperative was originally formed by farmers, ranchers, and local residents who banded together to obtain telephone service that commercial providers deemed unprofitable to offer.

The member-owned structure means a locally elected board of directors governs operations, and revenues above operating expenses are returned to members as capital credits based on usage. Consolidated’s motto, “Reach the World from Here,” reflects its mission to bring urban-level telecommunications to rural areas at comparable cost, driven by a commitment to honesty, integrity, and community service rather than profit.

The company runs 175 circular knitting machines in a 150,000-square-foot facility on 29 acres, with a production capacity of 2 million pounds of fabric per month. It offers both coarse and fine-gauge knits, supplying greige goods and finished fabrics. Its lint-controlled, humidity-defined manufacturing environment allows simultaneous processing of all fiber types. An in-house research and development team provides fabric analysis and works with customers on the latest fiber and technology trends.

Contempora serves brands, retailers, and manufacturers across performance and activewear, athletic and team apparel, fashion and formal wear, casual and career wear, intimate apparel and shapewear, and swimwear and beachwear. A noted client is Boombah, which credited the company with helping its transition to CAFTA-compliant fabrics. The staff also manages weekly container shipments to Central America under USMCA and CAFTA-DR requirements.

The employee-owned structure is cited as a driver of quality and timely delivery. The company emphasizes competitive pricing, short lead times, and sustainability initiatives including energy-efficient lighting, upgraded HVAC, and recycling of cardboard, yarn scrap, plastic, and paper byproducts.

name: Corbitt Manufacturing Company
old_description: Since 1948 we have supported the transportation, construction, industrial tool, farm and foodservice industries. We deliver the top-quality products you need, when and where you need it. Guaranteed.
about:
Corbitt Manufacturing Company operates from Paragould, Arkansas, where it was founded in 1948. The business began as a diversified contract manufacturer specializing in permanent-mold aluminum castings. In 2019, the company was acquired by The Greenbrier Companies and now operates as a Greenbrier subsidiary.

The 100,000-square-foot facility houses three CNC machining centers and three furnaces feeding multiple pour lines. Core capabilities include permanent-mold aluminum castings up to 75 pounds (maximum mold size 48 by 62 inches), CNC machining with wire and RAM EDM, grinding, broaching, and milling, plus captive support services such as fabrication, hot and cold forming, progressive stamping, punching, bending, and welding. The shop handles production runs from single prototypes to several hundred thousand units and offers in-house heat treating, assembly, and reverse engineering.

Corbitt serves OEMs in earth moving, mining, agricultural, electrical, transportation, recreation, food service, construction, industrial tool, farm, and powertrain/transmission sectors. In transportation, it produces dock cleats, transmission casings, manifolds, and railroad car parts. For food service, it re-engineered motor housings for garbage disposals to eliminate leakage. Electrical customers receive explosion-proof receptacles and power line connectors, while powertrain clients rely on the permanent-mold process for gearboxes requiring tight tolerances.

The company emphasizes problem-solving engineering, with a team that brings troubleshooting expertise to every project. Its in-house testing protocols enable fast-tracked deployment of parts to customer fleets, and it promotes competitive pricing across the full volume spectrum.

Inventory includes transmissions, engines, body panels (bumpers, fenders, hoods, doors), lighting, glass, mirrors, interior parts, tires, wheels, drivetrain and brake components. Thousands of cars and light trucks are pre-dismantled and shelved for immediate pickup or delivery. The facility serves both walk-in customers and commercial accounts across northern Utah.

Crabtree Auto distinguishes itself through its ARA Certified Auto Recycler status and membership in the United Recyclers Group, which requires adherence to quality standards for recycled parts. The operation’s long-standing slogan — “CLEAN - ORGANIZED - QUICK SERVICE” — reflects its focus on facility upkeep and fast turnaround.

old_description: CrossFire’s Bridgelet products provide the Chiplet to Chiplet interconnect currently provided by Interposers, but without the cost, complexity or availability limitations.  Depending on system requirements, Bridgelets can be either passive or active.
about:
Crossfire Technologies Inc is headquartered in St. Paul, Minnesota. The company focuses on developing chiplet interconnect solutions for AI infrastructure.

Crossfire’s product portfolio centers on three core technologies: Bridgelet, Direct Chiplet Input/Output (DCIO), and OmniDie. Bridgelets serve as an alternative to silicon interposers, providing chiplet-to-chiplet connectivity in passive or active forms compatible with industry-standard die-to-die PHYs such as UCIe, BoW, and Ultra Short Reach SerDes. DCIO streamlines the die-to-die interface by removing unnecessary ESD protection, large pads, and overpowered drivers, delivering a protocol-agnostic PHY that supports standard link layers. OmniDie enables the physical integration of multiple chiplets into a single ‘SuperChip’ that mounts directly onto a package substrate, reducing reliance on advanced packaging.

Its solutions are positioned for applications requiring disaggregated I/O, memory functions, and heterogeneous integration across product families.

Crossfire states that its Bridgelet approach eliminates the cost, complexity, and availability constraints of traditional interposers, claiming up to 50× smaller footprint, 10× lower energy per bit, and 10× lower upfront cost. DCIO is said to achieve 10× lower power, 10× lower cost, and 10× higher density compared to competing solutions.

about:
Custom Battery Cables LLC operates from Mesa, Arizona. The business was launched in 2003 by founder Vince, who began building cables for his own 1948 Willy’s CJ‑2A while studying diesel and heavy‑equipment technology at Maricopa Technical Community College. After a career as a mechanic for firms such as Mountain Bell and Sunstate Equipment, and a 29‑year tenure at Intel in electronics engineering, Vince started the company from a spare room in his home.

The shop hand‑builds made‑to‑order battery cables for cars, trucks, boats, RVs, golf carts, solar installations and heavy equipment. Cables are assembled to the customer’s exact length using SAE SGT, SGX or marine‑grade wire, and the company also produces alternator wires with fuse links. A team of seven — including a manufacturing manager, shipping lead, marketing lead and several technicians — handles production, assembly and customer support.

The primary markets are automotive, marine, solar, recreational vehicle, golf‑cart and heavy‑equipment sectors. Customers range from individual owners restoring classic vehicles or upgrading high‑output engines to commercial buyers placing bulk orders for fleet or industrial use. The company explicitly invites bulk inquiries alongside its direct‑to‑consumer sales.

Vince’s guiding principle, drawn from a mentor’s advice, is to “solve the customer’s problem” — whether that means fixing a hard‑starting snowplow or supplying show‑quality cables. The company differentiates itself by using heavier, higher‑grade wire than typical OEM or auto‑store cables, refusing to cut corners on materials, and building each cable to withstand extreme temperatures and demanding electrical loads.
